title: Preach always
hookLine: Franciscans are known for serving before speaking

lines: ALL THE BROTHERS: PREACH BY WORKS.
cards: A rule for a band of brothers has a chapter on preaching. It opens with a warning: no brother is to preach against the Church's ways, or without his minister's permission. So far, a rule about who may stand up and speak.
Then comes one short line that widens the whole chapter: all the brothers, though, should preach by their works. Not some of them. All of them.
The cook, the one mending a roof, the one sitting up with a sick man. The rule is the one Francis of Assisi gave his first brothers, and in that line nobody is left out of preaching.

teach.b: Francis didn't invent the idea. He found it in the Gospel. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven."
Notice who gets the glory: not the one shining. The light points away from itself.

teach.h: SHEW ME THY FAITH BY MY WORKS.
teach.b: The letter of James puts it with a shrug: "shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works." Words can say faith. Works show it.

teach.h: NOT IN WORD, BUT IN DEED.
teach.b: And the first letter of John says it tenderly: "My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth." That's the ground Francis stood on.

In the stories told about him and his first brothers, they work with their hands, they look after lepers, they sweep out churches. When they do speak, the speaking comes out of a life people have already watched.

Now, a fair word for the other side. The early stories have Francis preaching out loud too, in town squares as well as churches. And Paul asks how anyone will believe in one of whom they have not heard.
So, in this way of reading it, it isn't works instead of words. It's an order of things.

teach.h: THE LIFE FIRST, THEN THE WORDS.
teach.b: The life comes first and stays longest; words, when they come, have somewhere to stand. A sermon ends. A life is preached every day, including the days you'd rather nobody was watching.

how: Franciscan friars and sisters, and lay people who follow Francis's way, often serve the poor and the sick in quiet, practical ways, and speak of letting their lives bear witness alongside their words.

o: give a sermon in church every single week
repeat the same sermon until people listen
let your daily life show your faith

games.q: the life that preaches — tap the pairs.
p: all the brothers preach by works
shew me thy faith by my works
not in word, but in deed

s: Francis's rule asks only the brothers with permission to preach by their works
permission is for preaching in words. preaching by works is asked of all the brothers.
the early stories say Francis never preached out loud
they have him preaching aloud, in town squares too. the point is the order: the life first, then the words.
in Matthew, the light points glory away from the one shining
they see your good works and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

games.q: you're one of Francis's first brothers. you'll never stand in a pulpit. what does the rule ask of you?
o: nothing; preaching is for the ones with permission.
preach by your works, like all the brothers.
argue with people in the square until they agree.
games.why: the rule asks all the brothers to preach by their works. the ones who never spoke in church were still preachers.

practice: Let someone come to mind who could use a hand, a tired coworker, a neighbor, someone at home, and find one small thing for them: wash what they'd have to wash, refill what's empty, carry what's heavy.
Then settle the harder part: no hint, no credit. If you pray, you can offer it to God in advance.

wordCard.voice: Preach always. The heart of a line in Francis's rule: let all the brothers preach by their works, so the life speaks before the mouth does.

orig.note: Greek: to proclaim aloud, as a herald does; Mark 16:15 uses this verb for preach the gospel.

carryVoice: Your line: preach with your life. The light points away from itself. See you tomorrow.
